property_summary: The reference supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl regardless of super's result, but the bug returns true only when both are true, so it fails when super returns false for an invalid interface ID.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if the interface ID matches IAccessControl or super.supportsInterface returns true. The bug uses AND so returns false when the ID matches IAccessControl but super returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId regardless of super.supportsInterface's result; the bug requires both to be true, so it returns false when interfaceId matches IAccessControl but super returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the buggy version ANDs this with super.supportsInterface, falsely returning false when the interfaceId matches IAccessControl but super returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true whenever interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, regardless of the super implementation's result; the buggy version violates this by requiring super.supportsInterface to also return true.
The correct contract supports the IAccessControl interface (returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) while the mutant does not, breaking ERC165 compliance.

For any bytes4 selector, the correct contract returns true if and only if the selector equals the IAccessControl interface ID or is supported by the superclass, while the mutant incorrectly returns true only for the IERC165 interface ID.

For any bytes4 `interfaceId`, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true iff `interfaceId` equals `type(IAccessControl).interfaceId` or `ERC165.supportsInterface(interfaceId)` returns true; the buggy version omits the IAccessControl check and returns false for `type(IAccessControl).interfaceId`.
For every bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for that ID, violating this rule.
For every bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for IAccessControl's interface ID. The mutant omits this check and returns false.

The reference AccessControl-derived contract supports the IAccessControl interface, while the buggy version always returns false for any interface query, violating the ERC-165 requirement that a contract claiming to implement IAccessControl must return true for its interface ID.

For the reference contract, supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) must return true; the bug makes it always return false, violating ERC-165 and the contract's own explicit override that includes IAccessControl support.

For any bytes4 input, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true exactly when the input is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId, while the mutant always returns false, violating ERC-165 required behavior for the IAccessControl interface.

For the reference contract C, the expression supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) must return true; the buggy version always returns false, violating the ERC-165 requirement for a contract that inherits and overrides IAccessControl support.
For any role and account, `hasRole` must return true iff the role was granted to the account; the bug returns false unconditionally.

The reference C always returns the actual stored role membership for any (role, account), while the buggy version returns true unconditionally, breaking the invariant that hasRole returns false for an account never granted the role.
For any role and account, hasRole must only return true if the role was actually granted to that account, which the unchecked true return violates for any non-member.

The getRoleAdmin function must return the stored admin role for any role, but the mutant always returns bytes32(0), violating the invariant that getRoleAdmin(role) equals the actual adminRole set during construction.
After construction, getRoleAdmin for PROPOSER_ROLE should return TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE (the admin set in the constructor), but the mutant always returns bytes32(0).

For any role, getRoleAdmin(role) must return the adminrole that was set during construction via _setRoleAdmin; the bug always returns bytes32(0) for any role, violating this rule for roles that had a non-zero adminRole set.

For any role that was assigned a non-zero admin role during construction, getRoleAdmin(role) must return that assigned admin role; the mutant always returns bytes32(0), violating this for roles such as PROPOSER_ROLE.
